solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They don't think a bird is helpful outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the words for being helpful wrap round the bird

parts.note: is helpful means aids, as in assists
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a bird nearby is being useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of people, not a statement: those who don't think are the empty-headed. 'outside' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for empty-headed people, those who notably fail to use their brains.

clue.text: Purposeless commercial break

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An advertising break with no point.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting without direction or aim, figuratively aimless.

clue.text: Carpeting salesman on his travels?

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
roving means wandering, travelling about

explanation.surface: A travelling sales rep peddling carpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' suggests floor coverings, but to carpet someone is to give them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpeting in the sense of reprimanding, a British idiom for a scolding.

clue.text: Order raised in order to get downloaded work

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the honour's letters read upwards

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
OK means fine, in order

explanation.surface: An instruction is escalated so that a file can be downloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards, so the honour's letters come out as EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book, a written work one downloads to a device.

clue.text: Cleans with one's own cloth

parts.note: to do a room is to clean it
your kin are your own people, your family

explanation.surface: Someone cleans using a cloth of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft woollen fabric with a napped finish, named after deer hide.

clue.text: Mountain trail around region of India

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: around signals that the word for trail is turned back to front

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind

explanation.surface: A hiking path winds round a mountainous part of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the trail word backwards to give GAL; a Scottish ben is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic region in the east of the subcontinent, now split between India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Unusually nice, this marks pagan superstition

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: M stands for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An oddly pleasant thing that characterises heathen belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges NICE THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnicism is an old term for heathenism, belief in pagan religion.

clue.text: Creep up on a police officer

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us the creep word reads upwards

parts.note: to drag is to move slowly, to creep along

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks up on a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAG to GARD. A GARDA is an officer of the Irish police.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Garda Síochána, the national police service of Ireland.

clue.text: Long Island cat rescue?

parts.note: L and I abbreviate long and island
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A cat being saved somewhere on Long Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or support offered as a means of saving someone, a means of rescue.

clue.text: Wild eagles, primarily parrots, and other birds wrongly grouped

indicators.note: wild here means unruly, telling us to rearrange the letters
primarily means take only the first letter of eagles

explanation.surface: A list of wild birds, eagles and parrots among them, has been classified badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges E (first of eagles, via 'primarily') with PARROTS. The definition is fair because this old taxonomic order lumped birds of prey together and has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A former classification of birds of prey, since dropped by ornithologists as an incorrect grouping.

clue.text: Prince has rocky guitar line shortened

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of has are shaken up
shortened means the last letter of the guitar word is cut off

parts.note: a riff is a repeated guitar phrase

explanation.surface: A royal owns a shaky guitar part that has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges HAS to SHA; 'shortened' trims RIFF to RIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabic title for a descendant of the Prophet, used as an honorific for princes or nobles.

clue.text: Low rent primarily when put up in basic accommodation

indicators.note: put up in a down clue reads the pieces upwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of rent

explanation.surface: Cheap rent is a priority for someone seeking simple lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns MOO plus R upward to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single chamber to stay in, minimal lodging.

clue.text: Loud music is something to put on

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction for loud
rock is a genre of popular music

explanation.surface: Someone plays loud music as background.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress is a garment you put on, so the phrase describes it loosely.

clue.text: A barrow full of intelligence — a brain

indicators.note: full of shows the mound word holding the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound, and a knoll is a small mound or hillock
wit means intelligence or quick thinking

explanation.surface: A wheelbarrow stuffed with clever thoughts amounts to a brainbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrow' looks like a wheelbarrow, but it is the ancient burial mound, and 'full of' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone 'a brain' sarcastically suggests a smart alec who thinks they understand everything.

clue.text: Apple one leaves in place

indicators.note: in tells us the other pieces sit inside the word for place

parts.note: to place something can mean to pin it
I is the Roman numeral for one
leaves are pages, abbreviated PP

explanation.surface: An apple is sitting in its usual spot after a person has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a noun for book pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of eating apple, such as the Cox's Orange.

clue.text: Historian's family welcomed by priest

definitions.note: the 's is 'is': the historian is the name built from the wordplay

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the priest word

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest
kin is family

explanation.surface: A historian's relatives are greeted by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: C. Northcote Parkinson was the naval historian known for Parkinson's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: C. Northcote Parkinson, British naval historian and author of the law on work expanding.

clue.text: Wet trimmed timber carried by soldiers

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the word for soldiers

parts.note: men is a crossword stand-by for soldiers

indicators.note: trimmed means the first letter of the timber word is cut off

parts.note: a joist is a supporting timber beam

explanation.surface: A damp, cut log is hauled along by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts the head off the timber word, leaving OIST; 'carried by' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to dampen, which is a verb sense of wet.

clue.text: Flog antique door

parts.note: to thresh is to beat, as with grain
antique means old

explanation.surface: Someone sells off an antique door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like British slang for sell, but here means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The sill or entrance of a doorway, used loosely to mean the door itself.

clue.text: Sparkling silver fragments?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
litter is scattered fragments of rubbish

explanation.surface: Broken pieces of silver catch the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering, twinkling with points of light.

clue.text: Astronaut runs home after potty

indicators.note: after places the runs and home pieces behind the word for potty

parts.note: potty means crazy, as does gaga
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
in means at home

explanation.surface: A spaceman hurries back to base after needing the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' suggests a child's toilet but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri, the Soviet cosmonaut who became the first human in space in 1961.

clue.text: Artless dancing in a foxtrot

indicators.note: dancing tells us the letters move about

parts.note: Foxtrot is the NATO alphabet code word for F

explanation.surface: A clumsy, naive figure doing a foxtrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges IN A plus F.
explanation.definitionFit: Naïve and unsophisticated, lacking guile.

clue.text: Ring starts to break in time

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the word for time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A bell sounds to mark the beginning of a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes more than one opening letter here, BR, which some solvers find a stretch; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring of a voice or instrument is its tone colour, its characteristic sound quality.

clue.text: Pharaoh hiding head of grass snake in water tower

indicators.note: hiding means the pharaoh contains the other pieces

parts.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of grass

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king conceals a snake in the grass inside a water tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water tower' looks like a structure but is a vessel that tows on water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful boat that tows ships, read as one that tows on water.

clue.text: A row of houses bounded by railway and major road

indicators.note: bounded by means the houses sit inside the railway word

parts.note: Ter. abbreviates terrace, a row of joined houses

explanation.surface: Houses in a row hemmed in between a railway line and a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial route, a main thoroughfare carrying heavy traffic.

clue.text: This is not helping one married couple

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a pairing is a couple

explanation.surface: A remark that a husband-and-wife team is unhelpful.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaging or weakening something, the opposite of assisting.

clue.text: L for leather

definitions.meaning: L is the abbreviation of the ... sterling, from libra
to leather someone is to beat them hard

explanation.surface: L stands for leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is a unit of money abbreviated L; to beat is to thrash someone.

clue.text: Mask — guest doesn't need it

indicators.note: doesn't need tells us to drop the word it from the guest word

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A masked ball where a guest has no need of a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: VISITOR loses IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor shields the face, as a mask does, especially on a helmet.

clue.text: Important part of relativity rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the letters are turned back
part of shows the letters come from within relativity

explanation.surface: A key element of Einstein's theory is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: crucial, essential to success or to life itself.

clue.text: Scottish town where uranium's in short supply

indicators.note: in places the uranium symbol inside the rearranged letters
supply read as supple-ly, flexibly, signals reworking the letters

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A remote Scottish town where uranium is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is the adverb from supple, rearranging SHORT to THRSO around U. THURSO is a town on the far north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Caithness, the most northerly on the British mainland.

clue.text: Comment that's often too nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that is frequently too unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges OFTEN TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A note at the bottom of the page adding a remark to the main text.

clue.text: Small animal lair found among rubbish

indicators.note: found among means placed inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A creature's burrow turns up in a refuse heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnawing mammal such as a rat or mouse.

clue.text: Without feeling lost, moved slowly

indicators.note: moved signals the letters of lost are shifted around

parts.note: idly means lazily, without hurry

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost their way trudges on, numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges LOST to STOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolidly means impassively, showing no emotion.
